## LLM Recipe

### 1.3 Pretraining &amp; Optimization

#### [Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19419>)

A controlled study tests optimizer transfer from pretraining to short-horizon, teacher-probability distillation using four Qwen student–teacher pairs and fixed update budgets. Its evaluated matrix-structured recipes show no consistent advantage over AdamW or AdaGrad in teacher matching versus trainer time, giving practitioners a concrete protocol for rechecking optimizer choices in the distillation setting.

**Published:** 2026-11-14 · **First seen:** 2026-11-18T11:00:32.735+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Optimizer Transfer, KL Distillation, Fixed-Budget Evaluation, Training Costs

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Complete 12-page primary inspected: Sections 1–6, all implementation/grafting/hyperparameter Appendices A–C; actual Figure 1 p.5 and Figure 3 p.7 directly viewed. Qwen3 0.6B←1.7B, 4B←8B, 14B←32B and Qwen2.5 32B←72B share within-pair teacher/student tokenizer, 79,535 Nemotron reasoning traces, 1,006 validation examples, batch 144 and 1,683 optimizer updates. Training balances answer/reasoning region means equally using pure forward KL; validation averages assistant tokens, a distinct length weighting. BF16 FSDP2/FP32 gradient reduction uses 72 GB200 accelerators for Qwen3 and 144 for Qwen2.5; no weight decay, scheduler or warmup. Full-budget results use three seeds and descriptive mean±SD of per-seed best validation KL, plus matched-step trajectories. AdamW generally achieves lower KL; every completed structured recipe adds trainer time, while AdaGrad is slightly faster on larger pairs. Trainer time includes training, validation and improvement-triggered checkpoints, excluding loading/queue/export. The linked repository is the existing surrounding distillation framework, not a verified release of the paper-specific optimizer adapters: Appendix A says those experiments will be released. Native original LG RECENT Tuesday November 17 membership, sole-v1 receipt November 14 14:04:42 UTC, and official Friday14:00–Monday14:00 Eastern / Monday20:00 announcement row support inferred first manuscript announcement November 17 01:00 UTC. This is retrospective preparation of the November 17 report; actual first discovery is successful CL RECENT retrieval completion November 18 11:00:32.735443 UTC. Bounded exact-title/author-artifact checks did not locate an earlier full study; no first-ever-public assertion is made.

**Limitations:** Only four dense Qwen pairs, one reasoning corpus and a short three-epoch-like schedule; validation KL is teacher matching, not downstream capability. All-2D Muon applies its spectral update to embeddings/head as well as hidden matrices, differing from the standard hidden-only recipe. Shampoo uses two feasible unblocked right-factor reductions with an 8,192-dimension cap and diagonal fallbacks, not canonical two-sided family-wide coverage; SOAP is an unblocked replicated adapter. Hyperparameter pilots and validation-selected final configurations do not impose equal tuning budgets. Largest-pair SOAP has one 561-step run taking 4.31× paired AdamW trainer time and is excluded from full-budget summaries. Backend/routing/blocking controls change algorithmic recipes as well as systems behavior; no universal ranking, optimizer-kernel-only timing, causal explanation of transfer failure or independent reproduction is established. Specific experiment code is not yet verified as released.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.3 Context Engineering &amp; Memory

#### [MemDoctor: Stage-wise Error Attribution and Repair for MLLM Agent Memory](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21019>)

MemDoctor traces multimodal-agent memory failures through writing, updating, retrieval and answering, then uses versioned evidence to diagnose and repair the implicated stage. It reports net accuracy gains on two memory benchmarks, offering a debugging pattern for errors that can otherwise appear well supported by stored records. The extra checks can also damage correct answers, and they cannot reliably detect a wrong value repeated consistently throughout the available memory.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.6 Low-Precision &amp; Efficient Execution

#### [CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21584>)

CertiSum certifies when native MXFP4 matrix reductions are exact and repairs the remaining outputs, while preserving quantization blocks and exact accumulation across supported parallel layouts. In controlled 200-step Qwen3-8B experiments, parameters and optimizer states match bit for bit across MI350X and GB200 GPUs and elastic layouts, supporting stricter debugging and training audits. At larger evaluated shapes it adds 11.8–60.5% step latency over its non-exact MXFP4 twin; the guarantee depends on shared numerical contracts and does not establish BF16-equivalent training quality.

MXFP4 E2M1 products with shared power-of-two scales can be exact in FP32 when a runtime absolute-product bound fits its 24-bit significand and finite/range/kernel contracts hold. Quantizer statistics produce conservative certificates; uncertified outputs are not declared wrong but repaired through checked exact accumulation. Attention and most weight-gradient work are routed directly to exact kernels, accounting for 46–68% of nominal GEMM FLOPs, so the high native-GEMM certification rate is not a whole-training fast-path fraction. Fixed global 32-element blocks, 32x32 backward tiles, exact attention numerator/denominator and correctly rounded division require consistent non-reduction numerical maps. Qwen3-8B-Base/FineWeb-Edu plus Stack-v3 controls run 200 AdamW steps with full-state fingerprints. Cross-vendor TP4 divides output rows/heads, replicates weights/optimizer and avoids cross-GPU reductions; elastic MI350X 1→DP4→CP2→TP4→DP2 checkpointed segments preserve all states. Larger-shape timing on three 8B–14B models is 11.8–60.5% above its own MXFP4 twin, up to 1.24x faster than ordinary BF16 and 1.70x deterministic BF16; small TP cases can regress. Original LG Tue17 batch plus receipt Mon16 18:54:07 UTC and official EST schedule supports inferred first announcement Nov17 01:00 UTC. Actual earliest team discovery is the successful Recipe LG completion Nov18 11:00:32.762373 UTC; raw catalog and receipt copied and pinned. No earlier full release was located in the bounded primary/catalog/project search.

**Limitations:** Exactness is for the represented quantized computation under explicit contracts, not real-arithmetic or BF16 equivalence. Unsupported all-masked attention rows, altered block boundaries, arbitrary non-reduction operators or native-kernel behavior fall outside the guarantee. Shared RoPE/SiLU tables and host-assisted exponential/logarithm paths constrain deployment generality. Cross-vendor TP4 tests do not exercise reduction-sharded TP; inference validation is only 32 greedy prompts/64 tokens with repeated full-prefix computation, not a paged serving system. Timing combines implementation/layout/clock/graph differences, uses different BF16 reference training data/initialization in some cases and excludes specified outliers; it does not isolate certification cost. No convergence/accuracy-equivalence or RL-quality experiment. No matching author implementation was verified; dependency ROCm/aiter is not claimed as CertiSum code. No independent reproduction.

#### [NVFP4-MLA: New Quantitative Evaluation of Unified FP4 Cache and Attention](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18972>)

A new evaluation of existing TensorRT-LLM integration combines a shared two-dimensional FP4 latent cache with selective residual compensation so both MLA matrix multiplications run on FP4 Tensor Cores. On Rubin GPUs, the study reports up to 2.30× DeepSeek-R1 serving throughput over FP8 at matched per-user generation rates, with each precision using its best tested layout, while nine-task mean accuracy stays close to BF16. The 3.20× stored-cache reduction can help retain session histories, but it excludes decode-layout overhead and is not a whole-worker memory reduction.
